courses.title: Engine Mechanical Essentials
moduleTitles: Best Practice Head and Gasket Testing

questions.prompt: In a four-stroke engine, which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: One cycle needs intake, compression, power and exhaust - two crank revolutions, 720 degrees.

questions.prompt: How many crankshaft degrees does one complete four-stroke cycle take?
questions.explanation: Each stroke is 180 degrees; four strokes total 720 degrees.

questions.prompt: A relative compression test using starter current draw shows one cylinder low. What does that indicate?
questions.explanation: Less compression means less load, so current dips on that cylinder's compression stroke.

options.label: A
options.body: That cylinder builds less compression, so the starter works less hard on its stroke

options.label: C
options.body: That cylinder has higher compression than the others

questions.prompt: Before condemning low compression, which check helps separate ring leakage from valve leakage?
questions.explanation: If wet compression rises sharply, oil helped the rings seal, pointing to ring/bore wear.

options.label: A
options.body: A wet compression test - oil added to the cylinder

questions.prompt: A chemical block test fluid changes from blue to yellow/combustion colour. What does that suggest?
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Head and Gasket Testing
questions.explanation: The fluid reacts to CO2 from combustion gases entering the coolant.

options.label: B
options.body: Combustion gases in the cooling system, such as from a head gasket leak

questions.prompt: If a timing chain stretches, valve timing will generally:
questions.explanation: Stretch delays cam rotation relative to the crank, retarding valve events.

questions.prompt: A phaser-type VVT system changes valve timing by:
questions.explanation: A cam phaser advances or retards the whole cam by rotating it relative to drive.

options.label: A
options.body: Swapping to a different cam lobe

options.label: B
options.body: Rotating the cam relative to its sprocket

questions.prompt: A cam-changing (lift/duration switching) system primarily changes:
questions.explanation: It switches between lobe profiles to change lift and duration, not just phase.

options.label: B
options.body: Which cam lobe profile the valve follows

questions.prompt: On a shim-type valvetrain, clearance is too tight. To increase clearance you need a:
questions.explanation: A thinner shim leaves more gap between cam lobe and follower.

questions.prompt: On a rocker-type adjustable valvetrain, valve clearance is set with the piston at:
questions.explanation: Both valves must be fully closed on the base circle - TDC compression.

options.label: B
options.body: TDC on the compression stroke for that cylinder, valves closed

options.label: C
options.body: Any position, it does not matter

questions.prompt: The thermostat's main job is to:
questions.explanation: It stays closed during warm-up, then opens to regulate temperature.

options.label: B
options.body: Control minimum operating temperature by blocking flow to the radiator until warm-up

questions.prompt: Raising cooling system pressure with the cap mainly:
questions.explanation: About 3 degrees F boiling-point rise per psi of pressure.

options.label: B
options.body: Raises the boiling point of the coolant

questions.prompt: A chirp that changes with accessory load and a glazed, cracked belt most likely needs:
questions.explanation: Glazing and cracks mean the belt is worn; misalignment causes chirp and repeat wear.

options.label: B
options.body: Belt replacement and pulley alignment check

options.label: C
options.body: A shorter belt of any type

questions.prompt: An engine overheats only at highway speed. A likely cause is:
questions.explanation: Fans matter most at low speed; high-speed overheating points to flow restriction.

options.label: B
options.body: A partially restricted radiator or collapsing lower hose

questions.prompt: Pressure-testing the system and the cap checks for:
questions.explanation: A system that will not hold pressure leaks; a cap that vents early lowers boiling point.

options.label: B
options.body: External/internal leaks and whether the cap holds rated pressure

questions.prompt: The ECM turns the electric fan on mainly based on:
questions.explanation: ECT is the primary input, with A/C request as another common trigger.

questions.prompt: A fan relay coil tests open. The fan will:
questions.explanation: An open coil cannot create the magnetic field that closes the relay contacts.

options.label: B
options.body: Not run when commanded through that relay

questions.prompt: On an ECM-controlled (map-controlled) thermostat, the ECM can:
questions.explanation: A heater element lets the ECM open the thermostat sooner than wax alone would.

options.label: B
options.body: Heat the thermostat electrically to open it earlier under load

questions.prompt: Stray-current (electrolysis) corrosion in coolant is checked by measuring:
questions.explanation: Voltage in the coolant above a small threshold indicates electrical current damaging metals.

options.label: A
options.body: Voltage between the coolant and battery negative with a voltmeter

questions.prompt: A common cause of stray current in coolant is:
questions.explanation: Poor grounds force current to find a path through the coolant and heater core/radiator.

options.label: A
options.body: A missing or corroded engine ground strap

questions.prompt: Forced induction increases power mainly by:
questions.explanation: More air mass allows more fuel to burn per cycle.

options.label: B
options.body: Increasing the mass of air (and matching fuel) in the cylinder

questions.prompt: A turbocharger shaft is most commonly supported by:
questions.explanation: Most turbos float the shaft on pressurised oil films; oil supply and drain are critical.

options.label: A
options.body: Ball bearings only in all cases

options.label: B
options.body: Floating journal (oil-film) bearings fed with pressurised engine oil

questions.prompt: Blue smoke and shaft play after oil starvation most likely mean:
questions.explanation: Oil starvation destroys turbo bearings quickly; the root cause must be fixed.

options.label: B
options.body: Bearing wear - inspect/replace the turbo and fix the oil feed cause

questions.prompt: A twin-scroll turbo improves response by:
questions.explanation: Separate scrolls keep pulse energy and reduce interference, spooling the turbo sooner.

options.label: B
options.body: Keeping exhaust pulses from paired cylinders separate to preserve pulse energy

questions.prompt: A twin-charged engine combines:
questions.explanation: The supercharger gives low-speed boost; the turbo takes over at higher speed/flow.

options.label: D
options.body: A turbo and a larger exhaust

questions.prompt: Compressor surge happens when:
questions.explanation: Surge is an unstable stall - often heard as chattering when the throttle closes under boost.

options.label: A
options.body: Boost is too low at idle

options.label: B
options.body: The compressor is asked for pressure the airflow cannot support, so flow stalls/reverses

questions.prompt: Flutter/chatter on throttle lift-off can be reduced by a:
questions.explanation: Venting the pressure spike keeps the compressor out of surge.

options.label: B
options.body: Diverter/blow-off valve that vents or recirculates pressurised air

questions.prompt: A 48-volt electric turbo/e-assist mainly helps by:
questions.explanation: Electric drive spools the compressor at low rpm where exhaust energy is weak.

options.label: B
options.body: Spinning the compressor electrically to cut turbo lag before exhaust energy builds

options.label: D
options.body: Charging the 12V battery directly with boost

questions.prompt: The wastegate controls maximum boost by:
questions.explanation: Bypassing exhaust limits turbine speed and therefore boost.

options.label: B
options.body: Bypassing exhaust gas around the turbine

questions.prompt: An intercooler's purpose is to:
questions.explanation: Compression heats air; cooling it restores density and reduces knock tendency.

options.label: B
options.body: Cool the compressed intake air, increasing its density

courses.title: Engine Management Essentials
moduleTitles: Intake Runner Control Solenoid Type Diagnosis

questions.prompt: In port fuel injection, fuel is sprayed:
questions.explanation: PFI injectors sit in the intake port/runner aimed at the back of the intake valve.

options.label: B
options.body: Into the intake port, just behind the intake valve

options.label: D
options.body: Into the throttle bore only on all systems

questions.prompt: In closed loop, the ECM mainly uses which sensor to trim fuel?
questions.explanation: O2 feedback drives short-term correction around stoichiometry in closed loop.

questions.prompt: Gasoline direct injection differs from PFI because fuel is injected:
questions.explanation: GDI uses a high-pressure pump and injectors in the chamber, often 500-3,000+ psi.

options.label: B
options.body: Directly into the cylinder at high pressure

questions.prompt: A dual-injection (PFI + GDI) system uses PFI at low load mainly to:
questions.explanation: Port fuel washes the intake valves and helps low-load emissions; GDI dominates at higher load.

options.label: B
options.body: Reduce particulates and intake-valve deposits and improve low-load running

questions.prompt: A large positive long-term fuel trim means the ECM is:
questions.explanation: Positive trim = adding fuel because the system was running lean.

options.label: B
options.body: Adding fuel to compensate for a lean condition (e.g. vacuum leak, low pressure)

questions.prompt: Total trim (STFT + LTFT) near +25% at idle but near 0% at cruise suggests:
questions.explanation: A fixed vacuum leak is a large share of idle airflow but a small share at cruise.

options.label: A
options.body: A MAF fault that scales with airflow

options.label: B
options.body: An unmetered air/vacuum leak, proportionally biggest at idle

questions.prompt: Freeze-frame data records:
questions.explanation: Freeze frame snapshots key PIDs at the moment the fault matured.

options.label: B
options.body: Sensor conditions captured when a DTC set

questions.prompt: In electronic throttle control, if APP and TPS signals disagree beyond limits, the ECM will typically:
questions.explanation: Redundant, opposing sensors are cross-checked; disagreement triggers a safe default.

options.label: B
options.body: Enter a reduced-power/limp mode and set a DTC

questions.prompt: OHV cylinder deactivation keeps valves closed on deactivated cylinders by:
questions.explanation: Switching lifters collapse so pushrods do not lift the valves, while fuel and spark are also cut.

options.label: B
options.body: Collapsing/special lifters that decouple from the cam lobe

questions.prompt: Intake runner control changes effective runner length to:
questions.explanation: Long runners favour low-speed torque; short runners favour high-speed breathing.

options.label: B
options.body: Use a short path for high rpm and a long path for low-rpm torque

courses.title: Understanding Engine Sensors
moduleTitles: Hot Film Type Mass Airflow Sensor
Eight Wire Type Mass Airflow Sensor
Wire and Circuits Pull Up and Down Circuits

questions.prompt: The ECM calculates engine load for fueling mainly from:
questions.explanation: Airflow/air pressure, rpm and temperatures define how much fuel a cylinder fill needs.

options.label: A
options.body: MAF or MAP plus rpm and temperature inputs

questions.prompt: A healthy narrow-band O2 sensor in closed loop should:
questions.explanation: Switching shows it sensing rich/lean crossings around stoichiometry.

options.label: B
options.body: Switch repeatedly above and below about 0.45V, roughly 0.1-0.9V

questions.prompt: A wide-band (air-fuel ratio) sensor differs because it can:
questions.explanation: Its pump-cell current is proportional to lambda across a broad range.

options.label: B
options.body: Measure the exact air-fuel ratio over a wide range, e.g. 10:1 to 20:1

questions.prompt: A MAF sensor measures:
questions.explanation: Fuel is matched to air mass, so MAF is a primary fueling input.

options.label: B
options.body: The mass of air entering the engine

questions.prompt: A hot-film MAF stays accurate by keeping its film at a constant temperature. More airflow means:
questions.moduleTitle: Hot Film Type Mass Airflow Sensor
questions.explanation: Moving air cools the film; the heating current needed is the airflow signal.

options.label: B
options.body: More current needed to maintain temperature, which the ECM reads as more airflow

questions.prompt: An 8-wire MAF assembly commonly combines MAF with:
questions.moduleTitle: Eight Wire Type Mass Airflow Sensor
questions.explanation: Extra wires serve the additional sensing elements built into the housing.

options.label: B
options.body: Intake air temperature and sometimes humidity/barometric sensing in one housing

questions.prompt: In a pull-up circuit, the ECM internal resistor pulls the signal voltage up, and the sensor typically:
questions.moduleTitle: Wire and Circuits Pull Up and Down Circuits
questions.explanation: Many thermistor/switch circuits work this way: the sensor pulls the 5V reference down.

options.label: A
options.body: Pulls it down toward ground to create the signal

options.label: B
options.body: Shorts battery voltage to the ECM

questions.prompt: APP sensors use two (or more) tracks mainly to:
questions.explanation: If the two APP signals do not agree in their set ratio, a fault is set.

options.label: B
options.body: Provide redundancy so the ECM can cross-check for safety

questions.prompt: A TPS signal that drops to 0V briefly while sweeping the throttle indicates:
questions.explanation: Dropouts during a smooth sweep show a dead spot in the resistive track.

options.label: B
options.body: A worn/open spot in the sensor track - replace the sensor

questions.prompt: A coolant temperature sensor reading -40 degrees on a warm engine most likely indicates:
questions.explanation: On an NTC thermistor circuit, open/high resistance = the coldest reading; it also causes over-fueling.

options.label: B
options.body: An open circuit (high resistance reads as very cold)

options.label: D
options.body: A rich-only fault with no other effect

questions.prompt: In a Kettering (points) system, the condenser/capacitor across the points mainly:
questions.explanation: It absorbs the primary surge as points open, sharpening the magnetic collapse.

options.label: B
options.body: Reduces arcing at the points and speeds primary current collapse

questions.prompt: A plug with a worn, rounded centre electrode and wide gap will:
questions.explanation: A larger, worn gap takes more voltage to jump, especially under cylinder pressure.

options.label: B
options.body: Require higher firing voltage and may misfire under load

questions.prompt: Dwell is best defined as:
questions.explanation: Enough dwell saturates the coil; too little weakens the spark, too much overheats it.

options.label: B
options.body: The time/angle the primary circuit is on, building coil current before firing

questions.prompt: A plug lead with carbon tracking on its insulation indicates:
questions.explanation: Tracking is a leakage path that steals spark energy, usually under load.

options.label: B
options.body: Spark leaking to ground along a damaged/contaminated path - replace the lead/plug as needed

questions.prompt: A CDI system differs from inductive ignition because it:
questions.explanation: Capacitor discharge gives a very fast, high-voltage rise, common on small engines.

options.label: A
options.body: Stores energy in a capacitor and discharges it rapidly into the coil primary

questions.prompt: In electronic (transistor-switched) ignition, the module switches primary current based on:
questions.explanation: The pickup tells the module when to turn primary current off and fire the coil.

questions.prompt: In a wasted-spark system, one coil fires two plugs at once. The 'waste' spark occurs on the:
questions.explanation: Companion cylinders are at TDC together; one is on compression, the other wastes its spark on exhaust.

options.label: B
options.body: Exhaust stroke of the companion cylinder

questions.prompt: Coil-on-plug (COP) gives an advantage because each coil has:
questions.explanation: One coil per cylinder means long dwell availability and no secondary leads.

options.label: B
options.body: More time to saturate between firings and no plug leads to lose energy

options.label: C
options.body: Only one cylinder to fire at any speed with no control

questions.prompt: A coil pack secondary that reads open/infinite resistance most likely means:
questions.explanation: No continuity in the secondary means no complete high-voltage path.

options.label: B
options.body: An open secondary winding - the coil will not fire that output

questions.prompt: Advancing spark timing too far under load is most likely to cause:
questions.explanation: Too-early ignition raises peak pressure and temperature, promoting knock.

questions.prompt: Low fuel pressure with good pump voltage - the next mechanical check is:
questions.explanation: Pressure alone can mislead; a restriction or worn pump fails on volume under demand.

options.label: B
options.body: Check for a restricted filter, kinked line or weak pump, and check volume/flow as well as pressure

questions.prompt: Voltage-drop testing the pump ground while the pump runs shows 1.2V. That means:
questions.explanation: More than about 0.2-0.5V drop on a ground under load is excessive.

options.label: B
options.body: Excessive resistance in the ground - the pump is losing 1.2V it needs

options.label: D
options.body: Normal on all vehicles, ignore it

questions.prompt: An injector that clicks but delivers no fuel could have:
questions.explanation: Electrical operation does not prove hydraulic delivery; check pressure and spray/flow.

options.label: A
options.body: A clogged inlet screen/nozzle or no fuel pressure to it

options.label: D
options.body: A good spray pattern by definition

questions.prompt: Comparing injector current ramps, one injector shows a much lower, slower rise. That suggests:
questions.explanation: Current ramp shape reveals coil resistance and pintle movement faults.

options.label: B
options.body: Higher circuit resistance or a partially open injector coil

options.label: D
options.body: Low battery state of charge only

questions.prompt: A fuel pump control module varies pump speed mainly by:
questions.explanation: PWM control delivers only the needed flow, cutting noise, heat and current draw.

options.label: B
options.body: Pulse-width modulating voltage to the pump to match demand

questions.prompt: On a vacuum-referenced regulator, fuel pressure at idle (high vacuum) should be:
questions.explanation: Vacuum helps pull fuel through the injector, so rail pressure drops to keep the differential constant.

options.label: B
options.body: Lower than with the vacuum hose disconnected

questions.prompt: Fuel found inside the regulator's vacuum hose means:
questions.explanation: Fuel should never cross into the vacuum side; it also causes rich running.

options.label: B
options.body: A ruptured regulator diaphragm - replace the regulator

questions.prompt: Compared with pure gasoline, ethanol contains:
questions.explanation: Ethanol is oxygenated but energy-poor per gallon versus gasoline.

options.label: B
options.body: Less energy per gallon, so more volume is needed for the same work

questions.prompt: A flex-fuel vehicle knows the ethanol percentage mainly by:
questions.explanation: Content sensing lets the ECM adjust fuel volume, spark and cold-start strategy.

options.label: B
options.body: A fuel composition (ethanol content) sensor or calculated/virtual sensing from O2 feedback

questions.prompt: Running E85 in a non-flex-fuel vehicle is risky mainly because:
questions.explanation: Non-flex systems lack the trim range, sensing and compatible seals/hoses for high ethanol.

options.label: B
options.body: The system may not add enough fuel (lean running) and materials may not be ethanol-compatible

options.label: D
options.body: It disables the fuel pump relay

questions.prompt: NOx forms mainly when:
questions.explanation: High temperature and pressure combine nitrogen and oxygen into NOx.

questions.prompt: Unburned hydrocarbons (HC) rise most directly with:
questions.explanation: Fuel that does not burn leaves as HC - misfire is the classic cause.

questions.prompt: EGR reduces NOx by:
questions.explanation: Diluted, cooler combustion produces far less NOx.

options.label: B
options.body: Recirculating inert exhaust to lower peak combustion temperature

questions.prompt: EGR stuck open at idle will typically cause:
questions.explanation: Idle needs no dilution; excess EGR destabilises combustion.

questions.prompt: The EVAP system's job is to:
questions.explanation: Vapours are stored, then purged under ECM control instead of escaping.

options.label: A
options.body: Vent fuel vapours freely to air

options.label: B
options.body: Capture fuel vapours in a charcoal canister and purge them into the engine to burn

options.label: D
options.body: Meter liquid fuel to the injectors

questions.prompt: High CO on a gas analyser most directly indicates:
questions.explanation: CO is partially burned fuel - a rich-running signature.

options.label: B
options.body: A rich mixture / incomplete combustion with excess fuel

questions.prompt: A two-way (oxidation) converter converts:
questions.explanation: Two-way cats oxidise HC and CO; they do not reduce NOx.

options.label: B
options.body: HC and CO into water and CO2

questions.prompt: A three-way converter can reduce NOx and oxidise HC/CO at the same time only when:
questions.explanation: The 14.7:1 window is where both reduction and oxidation work together.

options.label: B
options.body: The air-fuel ratio cycles tightly around stoichiometry (14.7:1)

questions.prompt: A converter stores and releases which gas to work over the rich/lean swing?
questions.explanation: Oxygen storage smooths the swings and is the basis of efficiency monitoring.

questions.prompt: The ECM judges converter efficiency mainly by comparing:
questions.explanation: A good cat makes the rear O2 switch much slower/flatter than the front.

options.label: B
options.body: Upstream and downstream O2 sensor switching activity

courses.title: Understanding Diesel Systems
moduleTitles: Diesel Fuel Delivery Low Pressure Supply
Diesel Fuel Delivery High Pressure Supply
Indirect Glow Plug System Testing Procedures
Direct Glow Plug System Testing Procedures

questions.prompt: In a unit injector system, each injector:
questions.explanation: The pumping element and nozzle are one unit per cylinder - no common rail.

options.label: A
options.body: Only meters fuel, pressure comes from the rail

options.label: B
options.body: Combines pump and injector in one unit, usually cam-driven, per cylinder

options.label: D
options.body: Feeds all cylinders from one body

questions.prompt: HEUI injectors are actuated for injection pressure by:
questions.explanation: HEUI uses high-pressure oil to intensify fuel pressure inside the injector.

options.label: A
options.body: High-pressure engine oil acting on an intensifier piston

questions.prompt: Air entering the low-pressure diesel supply most commonly causes:
questions.moduleTitle: Diesel Fuel Delivery Low Pressure Supply
questions.explanation: Diesel injection cannot compress air in the lines; leaks on the suction side are critical.

options.label: B
options.body: Hard starting, stalling or no-start - diesels need a solid, air-free fuel supply

questions.prompt: On a high-pressure diesel pump system, a failed pressure control will most likely show as:
questions.moduleTitle: Diesel Fuel Delivery High Pressure Supply
questions.explanation: Injection pressure defines atomisation and quantity; control faults hit starting and power first.

options.label: B
options.body: Rail/injection pressure too low (hard start, low power) or too high (rough, noisy running)

questions.prompt: A two-stroke diesel gets its intake air mainly by:
questions.explanation: Two-stroke diesels cannot breathe on piston vacuum alone, so they are scavenged by a blower.

options.label: B
options.body: A blower/supercharger (and often a turbo) forcing air through ports, with exhaust valves in the head

questions.prompt: A diesel needs much higher compression than a gasoline engine mainly because:
questions.explanation: Compression ignition typically needs roughly 16:1-22:1 and healthy cranking compression.

options.label: B
options.body: Compression heat alone must ignite the fuel

options.label: C
options.body: Its fuel ignites easily when cold

questions.prompt: Glow plugs help a cold diesel start by:
questions.explanation: They pre-heat and often post-heat for smoother, cleaner cold running.

options.label: B
options.body: Heating the air in/near the chamber so injected fuel ignites reliably

questions.prompt: On an indirect (pre-chamber) system, one glow plug tests open with an ohmmeter. The likely symptom is:
questions.moduleTitle: Indirect Glow Plug System Testing Procedures
questions.explanation: That cylinder lacks pre-heat, so it misfires cold and makes white smoke.

options.label: B
options.body: Rough, smoky cold starting on that cylinder until it warms up

questions.prompt: For a direct-injection glow plug system, a current-draw (amp clamp) test is useful because it:
questions.moduleTitle: Direct Glow Plug System Testing Procedures
questions.explanation: Comparing per-plug current finds open or weak plugs quickly.

options.label: B
options.body: Shows each plug is actually drawing current/heating without removing the plugs

options.label: D
options.body: Replaces all other tests in every case

questions.prompt: White smoke and extended cranking on a cold morning, clearing as the engine warms, points first to:
questions.explanation: Unburned fuel vapour from cold cylinders is white; it clears with heat.

options.label: B
options.body: Glow plug or glow control faults (or low compression) on one or more cylinders

questions.prompt: 'Common rail' means:
questions.explanation: Pressure generation and injection are separated - the rail stores pressurised fuel for all injectors.

options.label: A
options.body: All injectors share one high-pressure accumulator (the rail) separate from injection timing

options.label: B
options.body: Injectors are driven by the cam only

options.label: D
options.body: There is one injector for all cylinders

questions.prompt: Typical common-rail pressures are in the range of:
questions.explanation: Modern CRD runs into the thousands of bar for fine atomisation and multiple injections.

options.label: B
options.body: About 5,000-30,000 psi (roughly 350-2,000+ bar) depending on system and load

questions.prompt: If rail pressure cannot build while cranking, a common cause is:
questions.explanation: The pump cannot build pressure if fuel leaks back or never reaches it.

options.label: A
options.body: A good high-pressure pump by definition

options.label: B
options.body: Excessive injector leak-back, a weak pump or a suction/supply fault starving the pump

questions.prompt: A key advantage of electronic CRD control is multiple injection events per cycle, used to:
questions.explanation: Pilot/post events cut diesel knock and support DPF regeneration.

options.label: B
options.body: Use pilot injection to soften combustion noise, main injection for power, and post injection for aftertreatment

options.label: D
options.body: Replace glow plugs on all engines

questions.prompt: The rail pressure sensor and pressure regulator work together so the ECM can:
questions.explanation: It is a closed loop: sensor feedback, regulator/pump control correction.

options.label: B
options.body: Hold actual rail pressure at the target for load and speed

questions.prompt: When a CRD injector is replaced, its code must be entered into the ECM because:
questions.explanation: The IMA/C2I-type code tells the ECM that injector's measured flow deviation.

options.label: A
options.body: The code is only a serial number for warranty

options.label: B
options.body: Each injector's flow correction/classification differs slightly, and the ECM trims delivery using that code

options.label: C
options.body: Coding changes the rail pressure mechanically

options.label: D
options.body: Coding is never needed on CRD

questions.prompt: Skipping injector coding after replacement can cause:
questions.explanation: Without its correction, that cylinder is over- or under-fueled relative to the others.

options.label: B
options.body: Rough idle, uneven cylinder balance, smoke or DTCs from incorrect per-cylinder fueling

questions.prompt: Swirl/throttle flaps in a CRD intake mainly help to:
questions.explanation: Air-motion control improves mixing, especially with EGR at part load.

options.label: B
options.body: Control air motion and EGR mixing at low load for cleaner, more stable combustion

questions.prompt: A leak-back (return flow) test compares injectors. One injector returning far more fuel than the others indicates:
questions.explanation: Excess return flow is a worn injector bypassing fuel instead of injecting it.

options.label: B
options.body: Internal wear/leakage in that injector - it is stealing rail pressure

options.label: D
options.body: A blocked return line to all injectors

questions.prompt: Leak-back is usually measured:
questions.explanation: Equal-time graduated bottles make the faulty injector obvious by volume.

options.label: A
options.body: With the engine at full power on the road only

options.label: B
options.body: At cranking or idle into graduated containers over a set time, comparing cylinders

questions.prompt: Diesel exhaust aftertreatment has to deal mainly with which two pollutants that trade off against each other?
questions.explanation: Cutting NOx in-cylinder tends to raise soot, and vice versa - hence DPF plus NOx aftertreatment.

questions.prompt: On a diesel, high-rate or cooled EGR lowers NOx but can increase:
questions.explanation: Cooler, diluted combustion makes less NOx but more particulates to trap.

questions.prompt: A lean NOx trap (NOx storage catalyst) works by:
questions.explanation: It stores NOx as nitrates, then a rich excursion converts it to nitrogen.

options.label: B
options.body: Storing NOx during lean running, then releasing and reducing it during a brief rich purge

questions.prompt: A DPF (diesel particulate filter) does what?
questions.explanation: Soot accumulates in the filter and must be oxidised periodically.

options.label: B
options.body: Traps soot in a wall-flow filter until it is burned off in regeneration

questions.prompt: DPF soot loading is estimated mainly from:
questions.explanation: Pressure before vs. after the filter rises as soot and ash restrict flow.

options.label: B
options.body: Differential pressure across the DPF (plus a model) - higher pressure drop means more loading/restriction

questions.prompt: A differential pressure sensor hose that is split or blocked will cause:
questions.explanation: The ECM trusts that pressure signal - a hose fault corrupts every DPF decision.

options.label: B
options.body: False loading readings, failed or unnecessary regenerations, and related DTCs

questions.prompt: SCR reduces NOx using:
questions.explanation: Dosed urea is the reductant that makes lean NOx conversion possible.

options.label: B
options.body: DEF (urea/AdBlue), which forms ammonia that converts NOx to nitrogen and water over the SCR catalyst

questions.prompt: If DEF runs empty or quality is poor, the system will typically:
questions.explanation: Emissions rules require inducement - warnings escalating to derate/no-restart.

options.label: B
options.body: Warn the driver, then limit torque/speed or prevent restart until corrected

questions.prompt: Active DPF regeneration cleans the filter by:
questions.explanation: Temperatures around 600C oxidise the trapped soot.

options.label: A
options.body: Washing it with water while driving

options.label: B
options.body: Raising exhaust temperature (often with post-injected fuel) to burn soot to ash/CO2

options.label: C
options.body: Removing and shaking it at every stop

questions.prompt: Repeatedly interrupting regeneration with short trips most likely leads to:
questions.explanation: The filter never finishes cleaning, so load climbs and fuel ends up in the oil.

options.label: B
options.body: Rising soot load, more frequent regens, oil dilution from post-injection, and eventually a forced/service regen or warning light

options.label: C
options.body: Instant engine failure in all cases
